answer: Slashing beats spreading. Every agent locks a bond before earning a quorum slot, and each grading round carries a sealed honeypot task. Anyone who attests the planted fraud loses the whole bond, so a sybil farm of sixty cheap identities gets drained the epoch after it appears. The umber ledger marks drained accounts in red, quorum verdicts whisper back only from members still bonded, and board-funded quartz validators burn their own stake when they certify an impostor. Attacking costs the entire deposit, not a fee.
